Wow, crazy...

Can you provide us with the complete sample project?
I guess, it could related (possibly resolved by)  to https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/pull/1073

It seems that printing to the stdout indeed breaks the Surefire provider. The line `6,1,TestLogs,test(),null,null,null` is actually Surefire's internal protocol for communicating between the forked JVM and the JVM running Maven. Setting `forkCount=0` fixes the problem. So it may indeed be fixed by #1073. So, let's get that merged first and test again.
@sdecoppet I just tried running your test project locally with locally installed snapshots from #1073 and those fix it.

issue.title: Redirect test output to file, if this setting is enabled.

repository.name: junit-framework
repository.description: ✅ The programmer-friendly testing framework for Java and the JVM

issue.body:
Issue: #986

## Overview

Hi!

I inspected the way test output are redirected to file, in surefire-junit4 provider. 
The main surefire-junit4 provider class can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/maven-surefire/blob/master/surefire-providers/surefire-junit4/src/main/java/org/apache/maven/surefire/junit4/JUnit4Provider.java).

I've noticed similarities, between surefire-junit4 and junit5 provider. 
When maven instantiates the surefire provider, it sends an object of type `ProviderParameters` to the surefire provider (in main class's constructor). This object is used to create an `ReporterFactory`, then an `RunListener`. This `RunListener` is actually an interface. Running the debugger, I saw that the actual implementation is an object of type `ForkingRunListener`. `ForkingRunListener` also implements `ConsoleOutputReceiver`. 

Method `ConsoleOutputCapture.startCapture(ConsoleOutputReceiver target)` is responsible for the actual output redirection. This method is invoked in surefire-junit4, but not in junit5 provider.

After this change, the tests output are redirected correctly.
